items.answer: Augmented reality (AR) is an enhanced version of reality created by technology, in which computer-generated digital content is overlaid on the real world in real time and registered in 3D, so the user perceives and interacts with the enhanced environment.
Mixed reality (MR) is an immersive technology that is the same as augmented reality, in which digital content is overlaid on the view of reality and can be interacted with.

Extended reality (XR) is an umbrella term, not a specific technology, that covers all present or future immersive technologies, such as augmented reality (AR), virtual reality (VR), and mixed reality (MR).

items.prompt: What is machine learning-based cybersickness evaluation (ML)?
items.answer: Machine learning-based cybersickness evaluation is an input-based cybersickness measurement technique that uses automated algorithms trained on psychological, physiological, or biometric inputs to automatically determine cybersickness, producing classification labels or a numerical sickness score.

Internet of Things (IoT) is a current stage in the development of computer systems in which users are surrounded by multiple connected computers that can communicate with each other without the user separately operating them, moving toward making technology disappear from the user's point of view.

Resource optimization is the technological optimization of resource requirements in extended reality (XR), including virtual reality (VR), that minimizes those requirements while maximizing immersive experience without compromising it. It generally focuses on client-end hardware so users can have a good experience with affordable hardware.

questions.question: What potential does computer vision have for augmented and mixed reality?
options: It can add enhanced interactivity for AR and MR
It can enable better applications for AR and MR
It can make systems scalable and affordable for AR and MR
It can integrate IoT, robotics, and blockchain for AR and MR
questions.explanation: Computer vision is positioned as an enabling technology for better AR and MR applications. The other options describe roles attributed to other technologies, not to computer vision.

questions.question: What do cloud and edge computing concepts help address in extended reality?
options: Better AR and MR applications through visual perception
More intelligent XR experiences through deep learning
Enhanced interactivity through generative AI
Scalable and affordable systems with better resource optimization
questions.explanation: Cloud and edge computing are relevant because they support scalable, affordable XR systems and resource optimization. The other options describe roles of computer vision, machine learning and deep learning, or generative AI.

questions.question: What is the current role of machine learning and deep learning in extended reality?
options: An enabling technology for better augmented and mixed reality systems
Relevant for scalable and affordable cloud and edge XR systems
Ubiquitous for better experiences and more intelligent systems
Used for enhanced interactivity in extended reality systems
questions.explanation: Machine learning and deep learning are currently ubiquitous for better XR experiences and more intelligent systems. The other options assign to them roles that belong to cloud and edge computing, generative AI, or computer vision.

questions.question: What can large language models or generative AI provide in extended reality applications?
options: Optimized resource use for XR systems
Scalable and affordable system architecture
Enhanced interactivity
Relevant IoT, robotics, and blockchain integration
questions.explanation: LLMs or generative AI can be used for enhanced interactivity in XR applications. The other options describe benefits associated with cloud and edge computing or with other relevant technologies.

data.text: Relevant extended reality areas not covered by the course are identified as paths for further learning. They connect the foundational course to wider technologies: computer vision for augmented and mixed reality, cloud and edge computing for scalable and affordable systems, and machine learning, deep learning, and large language models or generative artificial intelligence for better, more intelligent, and more interactive experiences. IoT, robotics, and blockchain also extend the set of technologies a learner can explore.
points: Computer vision is an enabling technology with huge potential for better augmented reality and mixed reality applications.
Cloud and edge computing concepts are relevant for scalable, affordable extended reality systems and for addressing resource optimization concerns.
Machine learning and deep learning are currently ubiquitous for building better extended reality experiences and more intelligent systems.
Large language models or generative artificial intelligence can be used for enhanced interactivity in extended reality applications.
Internet of Things (IoT), robotics, and blockchain technology are relevant technologies for extended reality applications.

questions.question: Why are cloud and edge computing relevant to resource optimization in virtual reality systems?
questions.reference_answer: Cloud and edge computing are relevant because virtual reality systems are part of extended reality, and cloud and edge computing are relevant to extended-reality resource optimization. Extended reality is an umbrella term that covers virtual reality. Cloud and edge computing are relevant for scalable and affordable extended reality systems and for addressing resource-optimization concerns. In virtual reality, effective resource optimization means minimizing resource requirements while maximizing immersive experience and balancing trade-offs.

questions.question: How do computer vision and deep learning differ in their stated roles for better extended reality applications?
questions.reference_answer: They are described at different scopes. Computer vision is an enabling technology with huge potential for building better applications in augmented reality and mixed reality. Machine learning and deep learning concepts are currently ubiquitous for building better experiences and more intelligent systems in extended reality.
